title: Grilled Street Corn with Cotija
seoTitle: Grilled Street Corn with Cotija | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Charred corn, creamy cotija finish
description: Charred corn, creamy cotija finish. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Corn on the cob, husks peeled

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Grilled Street Corn with Cotija in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Mayonnaise as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch vegetarian. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Char the corn
steps.instruction: Grill corn over high heat 10–12 minutes, turning until kernels blister and smell sweet. Do not boil first — you want smoke and char.

steps.title: Coat elote-style
steps.instruction: Brush warm corn with mayo, roll in cotija and chili powder, squeeze lime. Serve on sheet trays — street corn is best within 15 minutes but holds 30 minutes warm.

steps.title: Set up the station
steps.instruction: Stand corn in shallow pans for easy grabbing. Keep cotija and lime wedges in bowls for touch-ups — corn dries out under heat lamps.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F for any egg-based components. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Grilled Street Corn with Cotija onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Hold and refill
steps.instruction: Grill backup ears while the first batch goes out. Hold finished corn at 200°F up to 20 minutes; do not wrap in foil or mayo turns oily.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Grilled Street Corn with Cotija — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Grilled Street Corn with Cotija with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Grilled Street Corn with Cotija on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Charred corn, creamy cotija finish. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Grilled Street Corn with Cotija runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
